messages:
alex_k: Heads-up: preflight eval for summarizer-v3.2.0 showed a quality delta on the prompt-suite we gate on. @deploybot posted details below.

deploybot: auto-checks failed \u2014 metric: mean_ROUGE_drop = 6.2% (threshold 3%), sample fail rate 12/200. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/evals/1234 :warning:

priya: yikes. when did this start? is it localized to any route or dataset?

deploybot: Regression appears concentrated on long-doc summaries (>8k tokens) and the "policy-extract" prompt set. Top failing examples attached to the dashboard.

jamie: quick skim of the failing samples: most are truncation omissions, not hallucinations. looks like a tokenization/kv-cache edge for long-context.

product_sara: Given this is a user-visible summarizer, we should not roll full prod. Can we do a limited change-window push (EU window tomorrow 02:00 UTC) with staged traffic, or do we pin?

ops_marc: +1 to staged rollout. propose: canary 5% for 2 hours, monitor rouge and latency, then 25% for 4 hours. If fail -> immediate rollback to summarizer-v3.1.7 or pin on route.

priya: Can we run a quick bisect on the model artifact to confirm it's model-level and not conversion? I can run a targeted eval on v3.2.0 quant vs float artifacts.

alex_k: Please run that. If the bisect shows quantization regression we can push a fallback quant profile or promote a float build. If it's architecture-level we should pin.

jamie: If we decide to pin, we need to update release notes and the changelog BEFORE changing routing. ops, can you prepare the rollback command and a pin plan?

ops_marc: rollback/pin commands ready:
```
# rollback route to previous version
deploybot promote --version summarizer-v3.1.7 --route default --force
# staged promotion
deploybot promote --version summarizer-v3.2.0 --routes default:95,canary:5 --monitor eval-suite:1234
```

security_bot: Note: if we keep v3.2.0 in canary we must ensure we do not expose sensitive customer PII from the sample set in the failing examples. Confirmed scrub pipeline active.

priya: Bisect results: quantized v3.2.0 shows the same delta; float build is within threshold. Looks like quant profile caused regressions for long-docs.

alex_k: Ok that's actionable. Options: (A) apply fallback float build for now (higher cost) and proceed staged rollout, (B) pin route to v3.1.7 and delay v3.2.0 until quant profile fix. Which does product prefer?

product_sara: Option A (fallback float) is acceptable for the EU change window. We want the new features live but can't tolerate the quality hit. Ops, prepare float build promotion and cost note for finance.

ops_marc: Will prepare float build promotion command. Will also set abort conditions: mean_ROUGE_drop > 3% or error_rate > 1%. Implementing alerting to #incidents and paging if triggered.

jamie: I'll draft the release note snippet and add a note about the temporary float fallback and upcoming quant fix. Will attach PR to the changelog now.

alex_k: Thanks all. Plan: hold main rollout, do EU change window tomorrow 02:00 UTC with float fallback at 5% canary -> 25% if stable. If any abort condition hit, ops will run the rollback command. We'll mark the release as "staged-float-fallback" in the release metadata.

product_sara: Approved from product. :white_check_mark:

deploybot: scheduled promotion job created for 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z (job-id: jb-7741). Will post status updates in this thread when started and after each stage.

priya: I'll start the quant debug after the canary starts; hopefully fast turnaround.

alex_k: Great. If anyone sees unexpected regressions in the meantime, mention @ops_marc and we'll abort. Closing loop once canary completes. :eyes:
